#2564. Travis Kelce vs Rob Gronkowski GOAT debate settled for once and for all by Nick Wright

It's Travis Kelce vs Rob Gronkowski for the greatest tight end of all time, and Nick Wright has firmly hitched his wagon to one.

The NFL is largely marketed as a league for the quarterbacks, who are the protagonists, but some players not in that position manage to stand out.

When it comes to tight ends, Rob Gronkowski and Travis Kelce are not just two high-profile names, but they are genuinely great on the field too.

Nick Wright was asked who the "GOAT" tight end is, and he didn't hesitate before picking his guy.

Gronkowski has won four Super Bowls, and it can be argued that his single-season peak was higher than Kelce's, who is basically beating Father Time this season.

Having said that, there's something to be said about consistency and longevity, where Kelce has Gronkowski beat.

Both players have their own positives and negatives, but looking at it holistically, Wright, speaking on First Things First, believes that Kelce is the clear winner.

He said: "I think Gronk was the better blocker, but Kelce is so far and away the more dominant receiver. He's got almost 600 more catches, 50% more yards. Gronk does have more Super Bowl wins but Kelce is still playing and has one more playoff run in him. Maybe Gronk's single-season peak was higher but Kelce's the greatest tight end the league has ever seen. He's the greatest ever."

Kelce is likely to go to the playoffs this season barring a remarkable implosion, and with Patrick Mahomes silencing his doubters, something special could be brewing.

His relationship with Taylor Swift has almost made him underrated to the point where people forget how good a player he is in addition to being a crossover name in American pop culture.

A good playoff run this season could cement Wright's assertion that he's the greatest tight end of all time, and with good reason.

#2563. Monday Night Football: Commanders rally for 22-20 win over Bengals

The Commanders have wilted in the final moments of games at points this season, but they didn't do so on Monday night.

After a 56-yard field goal by Evan McPherson put the Bengals up 20-19, the Commanders took possession on their own 28-yard line with 46 seconds left to play. Jayden Daniels hit rookie wideout Antonio Williams with a pair of passes that covered 64 yards and exorcised the demons from their tie with the Giants by spiking the ball with time left for Drew Stevens to try a 26-yard field goal.

Stevens knocked it through the uprights and the Commanders were 22-20 winners on their home field. It's the second straight win for the Commanders and the end of a five-game winning streak for the Bengals.

Daniels was 23-of-35 for 289 yards and the Commanders scored on six straight drives after opening the game with four punts on four possessions. The final five of those drives ended with Stevens field goals, but the Commanders dominated time of possession in the final 30 minutes.

Their run game had a big hand in that. Jacory Croskey-Merritt had 13 carries for 54 yards and a touchdown and Daniels had a 47-yard run to set up one of Stevens's kicks. Williams led all receivers with nine catches for 122 yards, but the Commanders remained in position to pull out the win thanks to their defense.

The Bengals were limited to 124 yards in the second half and they punted twice after taking a 17-10 lead in the third quarter. Joe Burrow finished with 300 passing yards, but the big plays that were the hallmark of their winning streak didn't develop against a Commanders defense that limited Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to seven catches for 74 yards.

Washington improved to 4-5-1 with the win and they have to feel good about their chances of sticking around the NFC East race with games against the Cardinals and Titans on tap in the next two weeks. The Giants finished Week 11 at 6-3-1 and the Cowboys are 5-6.

The Bengals are now 7-3, which leaves them a game clear of both the Browns and Steelers in the AFC North. They split their season series with the Steelers and still have both games against the Browns on their upcoming schedule, but their immediate focus will be on next Sunday's game against the Saints.

#2562. Game Recap: Suns defeat Pelicans 123-119 in OT for fourth straight road win

The Phoenix Suns played their first overtime game of the season, as their battle in the Big Easy was anything but. They walked away with a 123-119 victory over the Pelicans, surviving a Jordan Poole variance magnet and extending their winning streak to four games, all of which have come on this road trip. It's also the sixth consecutive victory for Phoenix over New Orleans.

The Pelicans' bench provided quite the challenge, scoring 67 points and stealing the narrative the Suns typically own with the production of their second unit. Three New Orleans reserves scored in double figures, with Jordan Poole leading the way with 28 points on 9-of-12 shooting, including 6-of-8 from beyond the arc. Zion Williamson was the only Pelicans starter to reach double figures, scoring 25 points.

Meanwhile, four Suns starters scored in double figures, with Collin Gillespie providing 18 points off the bench on 7-of-11 shooting, including 3-of-6 from deep. He played the entire fourth quarter and overtime after exiting the game earlier following a scary sequence in which Ryan Dunn appeared to roll up on his leg.

It was a tight game throughout, featuring 19 lead changes and 12 ties. Ultimately, the Suns pulled it out in overtime, fueled by five points from Gillespie and four from Miles Bridges.

The Suns improve to 4-0 on their current road trip and will look to complete a clean sweep when they wrap things up Wednesday night in Houston.

Jalen Green was the offensive catalyst early for Phoenix, at least from a shot volume perspective. He accounted for four of the Suns' first seven field goal attempts, connecting on two of them.

Meanwhile, the Pelicans employed a strategy we've seen plenty of times before. Give Zion Williamson the ball on the perimeter, let him get downhill and attack the basket, drawing fouls and creating and-one opportunities along the way.

The Pelicans aren't a particularly good rebounding team, and neither are the Suns. In the first five minutes alone, Phoenix surrendered five offensive rebounds, which New Orleans converted into five second-chance points.

The first round of substitutions included Khaman Maluach, who immediately made his presence felt on the glass and recorded an impressive block on the physical Zion Williamson. His insertion into the game helped spark a 13-3 run for the Suns.

Ultimately, it was the New Orleans second unit that brought the most energy in the opening quarter. The Pelicans' bench accounted for 22 of their 35 first-quarter points, fueling a 14-3 run in response to Phoenix's earlier surge, including a buzzer-beating three by Jordan Poole to end the quarter.

The Pelicans carried that energy into the second quarter, playing with more physicality and pushing the pace, which was to be expected from a team that ranks in the top five in the NBA in pace.

Jordan Poole was feeling it, and I think we all know what happens when Jordan Poole starts feeling it. Either grab the fire extinguisher or body him up. Poole started his night 6-of-6 from the field for 17 points, including 4-of-4 from beyond the arc.

Still, the Suns had an answer for everything the Pelicans threw at them during Poole's heater. Halfway through the second quarter, Phoenix found itself with a 48-47 lead.

With 3:28 remaining in the quarter, Yves Missi went up for a dunk, and Khaman Maluach elevated to deny him. A foul was called on Maluach, prompting Jordan Ott to challenge the play. The challenge was successful, overturning the call to an offensive foul on Missi.

The minutes Maluach provided in the first half were spectacular. He was playing with physicality, and his hands have been looking much better as of late. Twice the Suns penetrated the defense and found him in the paint. Twice he caught it. Twice he dunked it.

The Suns outscored the Pelicans 25-19 in the second quarter. New Orleans shot 8-of-16 from deep in the first half, but their 11 turnovers allowed Phoenix to hang around.

The Suns surrendered only three more offensive rebounds than they collected and were outrebounded by two overall, although it certainly felt much different watching the game unfold.

Jordan Poole led all scorers with 17 points off the bench, while Dillon Brooks and Jalen Green each had 10 points. Khaman Maluach contributed six points and five rebounds in 10 minutes of action.

Heading into halftime, the Suns held a 56-54 lead.

The Suns opened the second half on a 5-0 run, and Pelicans head coach Jamahl Mosley opted to use a challenge after Herb Jones was called for fouling Dillon Brooks on a jump shot. The challenge was unsuccessful, although Brooks proceeded to miss both free throws.

Shortly thereafter, with the Suns leading 61-58, Jordan Ott utilized his second challenge of the night, disputing whether the ball went out of bounds off Jeremiah Fears following a Devin Booker block. The challenge was successful, and Phoenix retained possession. Both teams, however, were now out of challenges.

The third quarter was a back-and-forth affair, but one of the more painful moments came following a collision between Ryan Dunn and Collin Gillespie as they pursued a rebound after a missed transition opportunity by Zion Williamson.

Dunn was pushed into Gillespie, taking his legs out from underneath him. Gillespie exited the game and immediately headed to the locker room.

Jordan Poole returned to the game and continued to cook. After falling behind by seven points, the Pelicans rattled off a 16-2 run that included another Poole three-pointer, this one coming with a foul that was upgraded to a Flagrant 1.

It certainly didn't help that during a 10-0 stretch of that run, Jalen Green opted to go into isolation and chuck up an airball from beyond the arc.

The Pelicans outscored the Suns 29-23 in the third quarter, fueled by another 11 points off the bench from Jordan Poole and eight from Zion Williamson. Devin Booker scored 10 points in the quarter, but Phoenix trailed 83-79 heading into the fourth.

The fourth quarter started with a welcome site: Gillespie returned to the floor.

We once again saw a lineup featuring Dillon Brooks alongside the second unit, although Oso Ighodaro was out there as well. The Suns quickly tied the game, but the Pelicans continued to use their size to their advantage, continually attacking the interior and getting to the line. Derik Queen benefitted from this aggression, shooting 5 free throws through the halfway mark of the fourth. He hit one.

The Suns, after being down by as much as 6, tied the game on an impressive Jalen Green 13-footer and took a 100-98 lead on a Miles Bridges reverse. Housekeeping note: Upon review, a Luke Kennard three-pointer was ruled a two-pointer, so it was a one-point lead for Phoenix, 99-98.

Jalen Green threw down a beautiful transition dunk and buried a three to put Phoenix up 104-100. Then came the carelessness. Green tried to do too much, Bridges followed with a poor pass, and consecutive Suns turnovers fueled a quick 6-0 Pelicans run.

The Suns regained the lead courtesy of a Miles Bridges free throw and a Collin Gillespie layup. Saddiq Bey tied it at 107 with 46.3 seconds remaining. The next possession? A patented Devin Booker turnaround 13-footer. Splash. Jeremiah Fears tied it at 109 with 22.8 seconds left. Booker passed out of a double team, got the ball back, and had his pass intended for Gillespie intercepted by Herb Jones. The Suns never got a shot off. Jones missed his half-court heave.

The unit out there to start overtime? Collin Gillespie, Jalen Green, Devin Booker, Miles Bridges, and Dillon Brooks. Yes, the Suns were going small. On the opening defensive possession, Gillespie did a stellar job of staying in front of Zion Williamson, forcing him into a fadeaway rather than allowing him to get to the rim.

He then converted an and-one opportunity on the other end to give Phoenix a three-point lead. Miles Bridges canned a three-pointer on the ensuing Suns possession, extending the lead to four.

The Suns looked much more locked in defensively during overtime. Their closeouts were spectacular, and it felt like they were everywhere. Even though they continued to get owned on the offensive glass, the defensive intensity was there, highlighted by a possession in which Devin Booker ripped the ball away from Zion Williamson.

Gillespie then knocked down a 19-footer as part of a 10-2 Phoenix run in overtime to give Phoenix the 6-point lead.

New Orleans continued to chip away as overtime progressed, and Saddiq Bey threw up a Hail Mary three-pointer on a play in which it appeared he traveled, pulling the Pelicans within three points with 25 seconds remaining.

The Suns inbounded the ball, and New Orleans began playing the foul game, sending Miles Bridges to the line. He once again went 1-of-2, giving Phoenix a four-point lead. The Pelicans chucked up another three, missed, and fouled the Suns with 2.6 seconds remaining.

Phoenix secured its fourth consecutive road victory, defeating New Orleans 123-119.

The road trip ends on Wednesday night with a Thanksgiving Eve battle against the Rockets in Houston.

#2559. Clock operator robbed Bengals of one final play

The Bengals-Commanders game carries a small but not insignificant asterisk.

As ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk explained in the postgame show, the clock operator incorrectly ran the remaining four seconds off the clock during the game-winning field goal from Washington.

Yurk said two seconds remained when the ball hit the net. It looks more like it should have been one second.

Regardless, Yurk said the replay process can’t restore time when the next play isn’t a scrimmage play. (There’s also a rule regarding restoring time when there are fewer than two seconds left, and — with all due respect to Yurk — it appears that there was only one second when the ball hit the net.)

The bottom line is that the clock operator was slow to get to the button, and there wasn’t anything that could be done about it.

What would have happened if the Bengals had gotten one last chance? We’ll never know, because the person hired to keep track of the time handled it incorrectly.

Or, depending on that person’s rooting interests, he handled it perfectly.

#2558. Jose Mourinho rules out Bernardo Silva as future manager but backs Real Madrid star for SHOCK Benfica role

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has dismissed the idea of any of his current players stepping into coaching anytime soon, naming one notable exception for the boardroom. Speaking ahead of their Champions League clash with PSV, the Portuguese tactician boldly tipped Bernardo Silva to eventually become president of Benfica.

Mourinho has sparked intrigue over the post-playing career of Silva, backing the midfielder to eventually become president of Benfica. The Portuguese manager shared his prediction during Monday's pre-match press conference ahead of their Champions League clash with PSV at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Asked whether anyone in his current squad possesses the makings of a future manager, Mourinho struggled to identify a single candidate. Instead, he singled out Silva for an executive path away from the touchline, insisting the Portugal international is destined to run his former club rather than coach.

Mourinho explained that the youthful profile of his dressing room makes it far too soon to spot budding tacticians among the group. While he regularly discusses tactical details with his players to build confidence, he cannot see anyone transitioning into the dugout anytime soon.

"It's still too early to think about which players might one day become managers in general terms, because we've got a lot of young players and very few who are nearing the end of their careers," Mourinho said on the club's official website. "Bernardo Silva will be president of Benfica, but as for a manager, I find it hard to think of who that might be."

Although Mourinho ruled out immediate coaching successors in his ranks, his comments underlined the open communication he fosters at the Santiago Bernabeu. #2556. Rams open to free-agent ‘upgrade’ with just four receivers left on roster

When Sean McVay sends three wide receivers onto the field against the Packers on Wednesday night, he can look down the sideline and find exactly one more.

That's where the Rams stand before any practice squad elevations.

A veteran who can give Matthew Stafford another dependable target would help. So would a fifth receiver who can spell one of the first four.

Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua (12) celebrates a touchdown with head coach Sean McVay in Landover, Md., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Getty Images

Asked Monday whether the Rams would pursue a veteran free agent, McVay said, "We've talked about all those types of things," according to the L.A. Times.

"I would never rule out opportunities to upgrade," McVay said, adding that his current receivers did "a great job" in their last game.

There's room to agree with McVay on both counts.

Xavier Smith caught his first NFL touchdown in the win over Arizona. Konata Mumpfield had already shown what he could do in an expanded role, catching four passes for 93 yards and a go-ahead touchdown in Denver while Puka Nacua was sidelined.

Both have earned work. The trouble is how few players are behind them.

Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay leaves the field after defeating the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images

Monday's depth chart lists rookie C.J. Daniels on one side and Tutu Atwell on the other, with Mumpfield in the slot and Smith behind him. Neither outside spot has a backup listed.

The Rams have already had to reach outside the organization to get to four. Smith was on San Francisco's practice squad before Los Angeles brought him back when Jordan Whittington went on injured reserve.

At the trade deadline, the Rams had reason to think the numbers would improve. They passed on trading for a receiver in part because they expected Nacua and tight end Terrance Ferguson back this season.

San Francisco 49ers wide receivers Deebo Samuel, left, and Brandon Aiyuk take part in an NFL football practice in Santa Clara, Calif., Tuesday, June 6, 2023. AP

Nacua has since undergone knee surgery, Ferguson needs season-ending ankle surgery and Davante Adams is still recovering from hamstring surgery. Ferguson's absence also costs McVay a receiving option when he wants to give one of his wideouts a breather and put another tight end on the field.

Spotrac lists Brandin Cooks, Hunter Renfrow and Tyreek Hill among the available veteran receivers. Brandon Aiyuk could join them if he clears waivers after the 49ers waived him Monday, ending a lengthy standoff.

Availability on paper only tells the Rams so much. Hill's agent said earlier this month that the receiver was still awaiting medical clearance, and McVay didn't single out a target Monday.

A practice squad call-up can get the Rams through Wednesday. With seven games left and two expected reinforcements lost for the year, there's a job here for someone who can stick beyond one game day.

#2555. Lakers honor longtime PA announcer Lawrence Tanter

The Los Angeles Lakers honored longtime public address announcer Lawrence Tanter by unveiling a plaque at Crypto.com Arena on Monday, Nov. 23.

Tanter spent 43 seasons in that role for the franchise before his death at 76 on Sept. 23. Tanter had officially retired in June.

He had called more than 2,100 games, including 14 NBA Finals series and four NBA All-Star Games, during his tenure.

The Lakers played a tribute video during the game that included remarks from Lakers legends Michael Cooper and Mychal Thompson.

Fans were also given the opportunity to write messages and memories in honor of Tanter in the Star Plaza outside of the Lakers' home arena.

Lakers coach JJ Redick also shared some thoughts about Tanter before the game against the Utah Jazz on Monday.

"He's an iconic voice," Redick told reporters. "He made a mark not only on the Lakers but the NBA."

"The first time I ever got to play in Staples Center, the curtains dropped from the scoreboard and the music came on and you hear his voice. …  It just felt like I made the NBA. He was an integral part of what made this place so special."

The third-year quarterback and rookie wideout, respectively, hooked up twice for 64 yards in the game's frenetic final drive, which spanned 46 seconds. Williams finished with game highs of nine catches and 122 yards, which were also easily career highs for the third-round pick out of Clemson.

At 3-5-1, they remain two games behind the New York Giants in the NFC East but have the tiebreaker if they can catch them.

The undrafted rookie kicker out of Iowa shrugged off the elements to do the bulk of the scoring for Washington − perfect on all five of his field-goal tries and one PAT to account for 16 of the Commanders' 22 points. He drilled the game-winning 26-yarde on the game's final play. Stevens also held forth after the game in a captivating press conference and hilarious conference that probably only could have been pulled off by a green 22-year-old.

Trey who? The Cincinnati edge rusher, who entered the night with a team-leading 6½ sacks, bagged Washington QB Jayden Daniels three times – leaving Mafe among the league's top five in that department by night's end.

As speculation continues to swirl about the "Monday Night Football" tandem's partnership – and specifically the fate of apparent lame duck Aikman – the duo continue to deliver a professional broadcast every week that belies the apparent tension that exists behind the scenes and that the Hall of Fame quarterback continues to fuel when he's interviewed by other outlets between games.

It certainly wasn't a neutral voting party, but 100% of the three dozen tailgaters polled by USA TODAY Sports at Northwest Stadium prior to kickoff enthusiastically embraced Washington's new alternate logo, a gold spear infused through the Commanders' usual "W" sigil. The mostly black alternate uniform was nearly as popular amid its coming-out party … though Buck said the burgundy jersey numbers were hard to decipher from the "MNF" booth.

Cincinnati's loss reduced its lead over its nearest AFC North pursuers to one game while weakening the Bengals' playoff standing, where they are currently projected as the No. 4 seed.

Cincinnati's loss softened the blow of the Jags' Sunday loss to the Giants just a bit. By virtue of a superior record in AFC games, Jacksonville reclaimed the third overall spot in the projected AFC postseason field.

The field temporarily went dark three minutes into the third quarter – and with NFL commissioner Roger Goodell looking on from a suite. Fortunately, it was never a Super Bowl 47-adjacent situation, and the press box remained fully lit along much of the venue's secondary lighting, main scoreboard and ribbon panels throughout the interior of the stadium. After a short commercial break from ESPN, the field was again aglow … apparently after the building's lighting vendor re-enabled the main lights, which usually go down for maintenance on Monday nights.

Hardly ideal playing conditions given a slick ball and field, not to mention an inspired effort by Washington's defense – which prevented the presumed MVP frontrunner from setting an NFL record by accounting for at least four TDs (passing and/or rushing) in six consecutive games. Worse, the Bengals fell two game off the pace currently being set by the AFC-leading Buffalo Bills.

Cincinnati's receiver had a quiet night (5 catches, 31 yards) and lost the chance to match Hall of Famer Calvin Johnson's mark of snagging at least 10 passes in four consecutive games.

#2552. Diving deeper into Cavs 122-108 loss to Bulls: Cleveland’s defense finds a new low

The Cleveland Cavaliers can't get out of their own way. A poor defensive effort against a bad Chicago Bulls team that was on the second end of a back-to-back led to a frustrating 122-108 loss.

16 points on 4-of-12 shooting, 9 assists, 4 rebounds

Chicago's bench led the way. They scored just over half of the Bulls' points with 63.

Jones was the leader of this impressive bench group. He knocked down shots and kept the ball moving for a unit that got everything it wanted inside the paint and on the perimeter.

28 points on 8-of-17 shooting, 5 assists, 3 rebounds, 2 blocks, 1 steal

This was an efficient scoring night for Mitchell. He got into the teeth of Chicago's defense at will, which resulted in him taking 12 shots from the charity stripe. It was another impressive scoring night from Mitchell, albeit in a losing effort.

Anything bought from the links helps support Fear the Sword. You can buy the Browns throwback shirt HERE. You can also shop all of Homage's Cleveland gear HERE.

19 points on 7-of-13 shooting, 2 assists, 1 rebound

Hawkins was Chicago's highest scorer. His three-point shooting (4-for-10) helped open up Chicago's offense, particularly in the second quarter, where he scored 12 of his 19 points.

It's easy to criticize coaches for their rotations and closing lineups. I try my best to keep from doing so for a simple reason: coaches know much more about their team and players than we on the outside ever will. But sometimes coaches can overthink simple things.

Atkinson did that midway through the fourth quarter. The Cavs went into the final frame trailing by just four, but a slow start put the deficit at 12 with just over six minutes left. Atkinson panicked. He opted for an ultra-small lineup featuring Mitchell, James Harden, Tyrese Proctor, Sam Merrill, and Peyton Watson to try to kickstart the offense. Yet, it didn't do so. Cleveland scored just four points in the nearly three-and-a-half minutes this group was on the floor. This allowed the deficit to go from 11 to 14, which all but ended the game.

There's numerous reasons teams don't play with groupings that small. The defensive limitations are obvious. Lineups with no real size inside often struggle to defend the paint and rebound, although that wasn't necessarily this group's issue. Their problems came on the other end.

Size is helpful offensively as well. Being able to create space with on- and off-ball screens, along with the threat of rim pressure, keeps an offense flowing. There's more to spacing than just having shooters. Spacing comes down to having players in positions where they can score, while also forcing the defense to bend with your moments. If an offense gets too one-dimensional or lacks some of the skills traditional bigs provide, then the offense can get stagnant, just like it can when there's too many non-shooters.

Here, the Cavs offense ground to a halt. Harden tried to set high on-ball screens, but because there was no rim pressure associated with it, all this caused was a simple switch. Merrill found himself caught in the dunker's spot and in the paint a few times, but wasn't a threat to score from there. In short, there's only so much room on the perimeter for four shooters to stand. This is how you end up with four points and one field goal against the 27th-ranked Bulls defense in the most critical moments of the game.

Thomas continues to be a breath of fresh air for a team that needs something positive to get excited about.

Norchad Omier has consistently brought the energy and effort the Cavs need. Plays like this show how he can change the momentum in a game.

The Bulls scored 22 second-chance points, due to retrieving 35.8% of their missed shots (77th percentile).

Rebounding often comes down to being in the right position. The Cavs' defense is constantly out of position, which leaves opposing players alone for offensive rebounding opportunities. That happened once again, against a Bulls team that is 15th in creating second-chance opportunities.

"Just effort. I think a lot of it comes down to how we start the games and the approach we take to the games. A lot of those mistakes that we made early defensively just have to do with our effort. That's the number one thing we have to address."

– Peyton Watson on what's wrong with the Cavs' defense

The second quarter was a microcosm of what has been wrong with the Cavs all season. The Bulls scored 45 points in that quarter alone, with a majority of those coming from the bench unit of one of the worst teams in the league. However, you don't need to be the 2016 Golden State Warriors to light up this defense. You just need one person who can dribble the ball inside the three-point arc, and the entire defense collapses.

It's impossible to have a good defense if you can't contain the ball. The Cavs can't do that right now. They constantly find themselves in rotation due to the help defense needing to step up. They compound this by not being quick with rotations. The guy beaten off the dribble doesn't rotate over to where the help defense just came from, leaving the backside defense at a disadvantage. If you have a team that's willing to make the extra pass like Chicago was, you'll probably end up with open shots like the Bulls had repeatedly.

Being without Evan Mobley has obviously hurt this defense. His presence alone would go a long way in making this unit more competent, but he can't fix everything.

The Cavs defense is broken. Their system doesn't work, they are weak at the point of attack, and the effort isn't there to make up for it. There aren't many reasons at this point to believe that they can be passable on that end — they're now 21st in defensive rating — let alone good enough to be actual title contenders.

Cleveland came into the season with the goal of being a top five defense. We're still early into the year, but we can safely say that won't happen.

Consistency has been an issue through their first 18 games. That will continue to be a problem unless the defense can turn things around. You can't rely on your offense to outscore your opponent every night, even against a bad team like Chicago.

#2549. Lakers use fourth quarter run to win weekly match-up with Jazz

A fourth quarter run saw the Lakers open up a double-digit lead that they carried to a 109-94 win over the Jazz on Friday.

After another back-and-forth affair against Utah through three quarters, the Lakers turned it up a notch in the final frame. In total, it was a 15-3 run that saw LA jump ahead 93-80, an advantage they carried to the final buzzer.

Employing a zone defense for much of the night, the Lakers turned Utah over 16 times, leading to 20 points. That helped them overcome a poor shooting night as they went just 12-41 from three.

Luka Dončić got off to a hot start, scoring 11 of their first 13 points. Jake LaRavia was the only other Laker to score on a dunk, which came off an assist from Luka. Ace Bailey was leading the Jazz with four points.

Thanks to Luka fast start, the team shot 57% from the field.

He wasn't just scoring, but was also connecting with teammates on shots. Cameron Carr had a productive showing off the bench, draining a triple and scoring five points.

Los Angeles ended the quarter shooting 52% from the field and were up by 10.

The Lakers did not have a particularly good start to the second period, going 2-9 from the field. Matisse Thybulle had the only points in the quarter. He was also one of the main reasons defensively why Los Angeles remained in the lead despite the slow offensive start.

Utah wasn't shooting great either, going 4-15 from the field. LaRavia and Thybulle continued their strong play, combining for six more points.

Kyle Filipowski had a nice showing off the bench for the Jazz, scoring 10 points. He was their only double-digit scorer.

Unfortunately for Luka, he picked up his fourth foul.

The purple and gold had built a 16-point lead, but on the shoulders of rookie Darryn Peterson, Utah chipped away, cutting the deficit to 11 at halftime.

The third period began with LA on a five-minute scoring drought as Utah kept inching closer. Luka stopped the drought with a midrange jumper, but the Jazz kept their feet on the gas pedal, led by Josh Green draining two triples.

Los Angeles was forced to call a timeout as Utah took the lead after a 3-pointer. Out of the break, Thybulle knocked down a triple.

LaRavia once again came up big, scoring four in a row to put LA back in the lead. It didn't last long, though, as Utah kept pace and tied it back up. Green now had eight points for the Jazz.

Utah was on an extended 25-12 scoring run.

Williams was fouled from behind the arc, made the shot, and converted on the four-point play. Carr added another four points to his strong night, giving nine total.

The Lakers were up by one at the end of the third.

Extending from the end of the third, LA were on an 11-0 scoring run to start the final frame. They opened up a double-digit lead. Thybulle scored the first basket of the quarter for the team, pushing his point total to 11.

The run extended to 17-3, and Los Angeles was up by 13 with 7:31 left.

George tried to get the Jazz going, putting up six points, but LA did a great job keeping the lead and keeping the pace where they wanted, not allowing Utah to make a run.

LaRavia knocked down a triple, his second of the night. He had a productive 15 points. With 1:28 left, Utah waved the white flag and subbed in their bench.

Luka finished with 28 points, four rebounds and eight assists. Kessler once again had a slow offensive showing against his old team, logging 10 points with 12 rebounds and two blocks. LaRavia had 15 points with 10 rebounds.

Thybulle continued his stretch of exceptional thievery with two steals to go along with 14 points and two blocks. Carr had his best showing of the season with nine points. Grimes pitched in with nine points and eight assists.

Williams ended with nine points and four rebounds. Sexton tallied 12 points and four assists.

The Lakers' next game will be against the San Antonio Spurs on Friday at 6:30 PM PT.

You can follow Karin on Twitter at @KarinAbcarians.

#2548. NFL Power Rankings entering Week 12: Is it time to start taking the Giants seriously?

NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North: Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

Before Week 11, the New York Giants had a perception problem.

They hadn't beaten a team with a winning record. Their advanced metrics said they were a below-average team. Their point differential was +7, which was meager for a 5-3-1 team. They looked like a team lucky to be playing in the putrid NFC East.

Then on Sunday, the Giants got a win that can help legitimize their start. They beat a Jaguars team that was a major buyer at the trade deadline and looked like one of the NFL's elite teams. It was easily the Giants' biggest win this season, and for a team that has missed the playoffs eight of the past nine seasons, one of their biggest victories in many years. It might change what is being said about the Giants.

"We don't really worry about that, we don't really care what they think or what they say," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the game, via the team's transcripts. "It's not our concern how we're evaluated. It's our concern how we play."

Yet, they knew what was being said about them.

"They keep saying we can't beat these teams, we can't beat them. I don't know why they're saying that," edge rusher Abdul Carter said, according to Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein. "But what are they going to say now?"

The Giants' upset win over the Jaguars changes things. It boosts their chances of making the playoffs as a division champion. The way the Giants' defense played, holding the Jaguars without a touchdown for the first three quarters, gives hope of a strong finish to the year after a first half of the season that lacked a quality win. The offense is still not great, ranking 22nd in DVOA. But J.J. McCarthy makes a few plays each game that also provide some optimism, Malik Nabers is one of the NFL's best receivers, Isaiah Likely is having a breakout season and Cam Skattebo generally provides at least a reasonable run game.

The Giants likely aren't going to challenge the 49ers or whoever wins the NFC North for a Super Bowl spot. But their start to the season has more weight behind it after beating a good team.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 11:

The 49ers have faced the No. 1 defense in DVOA (Seattle) and the No. 1 defense in EPA allowed per play (Minnesota). They scored 32 points against the Seahawks and 35 against the Vikings. They got a defensive touchdown in each game but it seems like no defense can hold down the 49ers this season.

While the offense has been fantastic, the 49ers wouldn't be the best team in football through Week 11 without their defense, which has excelled despite Nick Bosa not having a sack all season (he did have two quarterback hits on Sunday night). The 49ers have given up 17 or fewer points in six of their 10 games. They have given up fewer than 300 yards in six games too. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, who replaced Robert Saleh, is doing an excellent job.

The Bills have given up 37 points in four games since their bye. Of course, they have faced an incredibly fortunate run of backup quarterbacks, including Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Cade Klubnik (who replaced an injured Geno Smith in the second half) and Kyle McCord. Still, they have not given up a touchdown in 43 straight drives, the longest streak during a season since the 2019 Patriots, according to the Bills' site. That makes the Thanksgiving primetime matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs one that will help shape this NFL season. Is the Bills' defensive improvement real or because of facing inept quarterbacks?

The Bills' defense struggled early, allowing at least 29 points in five of Buffalo's first six games. The only team to not reach 29 points was the Chargers, who are currently 1-9. But the Bills felt like they weren't far off.

"When teams were scoring on us, I felt like we were playing good ball," Bills defensive end Greg Rousseau said, via the team's site. "We just had to clean up a couple things here and there. We were playing good ball. We weren't really finishing games at the end of the games."

The Bears haven't trailed in five straight games, and that streak brings back memories of the greatest team in franchise history. The last time the Bears went five games without trailing was 1985, when they went the final three games of the regular season and the first two playoff games without trailing, according to Larry Mayer of ChicagoBears.com. The Bears briefly trailed the Patriots 3-0 in Super Bowl XX before winning 46-10.

While this version of the Bears is much different than the famous 1985 team, their pass rush is starting to emerge since Jeffery Simmons came aboard in a trade. On Sunday, they sacked the Saints' Tyler Shough six times (three times by Simmons) and had 24 pressures, which is the most for the team since 2018, according to Next Gen Stats. The defensive improvement will be tested on Thanksgiving in a massive NFC North game against the Lions.

Very good teams are allowed to lose games, even ones in which they're favored. But the teams now ahead of them in the rankings haven't taken many losses, and now the Jaguars have three after a miserable performance in a defeat to the Giants on Sunday. Their chances to get the No. 1 seed in the AFC dropped to 1.6% after Sunday, according to DVOA.

The Jaguars can rightfully complain that a questionable call cost Parker Washington a touchdown. But the offensive issues for the first three quarters are what ultimately cost them the game. The Jaguars, whose offense had been very good before Sunday, had just one drive longer than 23 yards in the first three quarters and didn't score a touchdown. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen took responsibility, saying his plan "maybe had too many things in, moving parts."

"That's a direct reflection of me, and making sure that these guys are prepared well enough," Coen said, via the team's site. "We had been prepared in the majority of our football games, I felt like, and that did not show tonight, especially early on. I put that directly on me."

The Chiefs scored on all five of their first-half drives against the Cardinals, quickly putting away a poor and injured team. One of the stars of the game was tight end Travis Kelce, who is having a remarkable season at age 37. He has 586 yards and four touchdowns, two of which came Sunday against Arizona. His 58.6 yards per game is his most since 2023. There were only three instances of a tight end having more than 400 yards at age 37, and Kelce is already second on that list behind Tony Gonzalez and his 859 yards in 2013. Kelce is on pace for 996 yards.

There were conversations that Kelce could retire after each of the past two seasons, but he's still one of the most productive tight ends in the game. That helps a Chiefs offense that is fourth in EPA per play.

It was a typical Broncos win and not the blowout the 38-24 score indicates. They were outgained 370-351 by the Raiders. Las Vegas rallied to tie the game at 17 after falling behind 17-0 and had the ball at the two-minute warning, down seven points. A pick-6 by Ja'Quan McMillian put the game away in the Broncos' favor.

The best part of the win for the Broncos was perhaps finding an offensive identity. Rookie Jonah Coleman has taken over the backfield, and he had 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 rushing attempts Sunday.

"It's not easy, but he's responded really well to his situation," quarterback Bo Nix said, according to the team's transcripts. "He's been given a great opportunity with RJ Harvey getting hurt (knee) and having a few weeks off. ... It was an impressive performance getting that many carries, running the ball hard."

The Bengals have leaned into being a one-dimensional offense, and it hurt them Monday in a road loss to the Commanders. Washington got consistent pressure on Joe Burrow, including on some well-timed blitzes, and that was partly because it didn't have to worry about Cincinnati's running game. The Bengals rushed 14 times for 31 yards and threw it 40 times. When the Bengals got into field-goal range in the final two minutes, they couldn't run for a first down to grind out the remainder of the clock. They passed on second and third downs and couldn't pick it up. That allowed the Commanders 46 seconds, which they used to drive for a game-winning field goal.

The Bengals should lean on Burrow, who is still tracking to win an MVP after 300 yards and two touchdowns on Monday night. But the lack of a running game, and even the lack of any attempt to try it, could be a big problem for the Bengals in the playoffs.

Detroit's first defensive test without Aidan Hutchinson went well. The Lions allowed just 274 yards and 21 points, and Tampa Bay got 65 yards and a touchdown on a meaningless drive at the end of a game when Detroit led by 17 points. The Lions had four sacks, which was a good sign. The Lions' defense has been much better since the first few weeks of the season, and Sunday's game was without Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell.

The test Thursday will be tougher, with the Chicago Bears coming in with first place in the NFC North on the line. But if Detroit's defense can maintain this level, the Lions might be a Super Bowl contender. That could reveal itself on Thanksgiving.

"Our guys are competitive, man, and they don't want to be counted out," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said of the defense's performance Sunday, via the team's site. "And nobody cares. There are no excuses. And the only way to gain respect is just go about your business, man, and make plays and play together and prove your worth, man."

What we learned about the Vikings on Sunday night, mostly, was that the 49ers are on a much different tier. That's OK, because the 49ers are on a higher tier than all but a few teams.

The blitz was impervious to the 49ers' offense. Minnesota blitzed on 88.9% of San Francisco's dropbacks, and Brock Purdy was 19-of-23 passing for 231 yards and two touchdowns on those plays, according to Pro Football Focus.

"It's one of those things where I told our team, you know, when you play a good team like that and you don't play your best, you're going to get beat," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said, according to the team's site.

That hadn't happened before to the Vikings' defense and is unlikely to repeat, but now Minnesota has to adjust after its worst defensive day of the season.

The NFC West race is probably over, with the 49ers leading it by three games, but Seattle has a shot to make it interesting. The Seahawks play at the 49ers in Week 12 and there's an opportunity to at least make the race interesting.

The big story will be Sam Darnold, whether he can return from injury and how well he plays. The Seahawks are not entertaining the idea of replacing him with Drew Lock. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald defended Darnold, pointing out that he has been injured for most of the season, starting with the first game.

"The beginning of the year for Sam has been a tough road," Macdonald said on Seattle Sports 710, via the team's site. "I can't wait for him to be fully healthy, probably for the first time — minimal times it's happened this year — and get a full week's worth of work and we'll rock and roll from there."

The dream of getting Puka Nacua back for a playoff run is dead, after Nacua had knee surgery that will keep him out the rest of the season. Davante Adams should return but the Rams' offense won't be what was expected before the season, when expectations were sky high.

Even making the playoffs will be difficult because of the Rams' challenging upcoming schedule. Their playoff odds are down to 38.1%, according to DVOA. The Rams practically need a win Wednesday over the Packers, who are one of their main competitors in a very tough NFC wild-card race.

Micah Parsons is set to return for the Packers after practicing in pads Sunday. It's major news for Green Bay to add one of the NFL's best players to the lineup. The Packers were 9-3-1 and leading in the second half at Denver when Parsons tore his ACL last season.

Wednesday at the Rams is a massive game for the Packers and their playoff hopes, and there will be the temptation to play Parsons more than he's ready for in his return. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur is aware of that issue.

"I never wanna place limitations on anybody, but he hasn't played football in a long time," LaFleur said, via Athlon Sports. "So, I think you've got to be conscious of that, and there's probably going to be plays that don't look like him, and there's going to be some plays that do."

Perhaps the biggest development for the Giants on Sunday was defensive end Abdul Carter picking up two sacks. Production had been surprisingly thin for the third overall pick of the 2025 NFL Draft. He had just six sacks in 26 games before Sunday, though his underlying metrics said that sacks were bound to come. Carter also had five quarterback hits.

Carter came in as an elite prospect and if he can start translating his pass rush success into sacks, that could be huge for the Giants. That happened Sunday as the defense played very well against a good Jaguars offense.

"As a defense, we showed what we really about," Carter told CBS after the game. "And for me, I'm the best in the world."

Seeing the Raiders' upset bid fall short was good news for the Browns. Their game against Las Vegas in Week 12, which got flexed to Sunday night, would have been much more interesting in the wild-card race had the Raiders been 5-6 instead of 4-7. It also wasn't bad for Cleveland to see the Steelers slip back to 6-4 with a bad loss at Philadelphia.

The Browns aren't a lock to make the playoffs but the path is very clear. They have two games left against the Bengals and one against the Giants, but the other four are against teams with losing records.

The biggest game in the NFC South this season comes in Tampa Bay next Monday night. The Panthers face the Buccaneers. Tampa Bay gets the season sweep and the tiebreaker with the win. The Falcons and Saints aren't completely out of the running, but Carolina and Tampa Bay look like the two best teams in a bad division.

An old problem popped up again, and it was the run defense. Baltimore had 157 rushing yards, averaging 7.1 yards per attempt. That's a bad weakness to have against the Buccaneers, who lead the NFL at 5 yards per carry.

"They had way too many yards today. Takeaways and stuff is cool, but we got to stop them in the run game," linebacker Tyrel Dodson told the team's site.

The Steelers were showing improvement but the last two weeks are alarming. They were destroyed by the Bengals, then didn't threaten an Eagles team that had lost seven in a row and was on its third quarterback this season. The lingering problem from the game is receiver DK Metcalf getting ejected after another unproductive game. The NFL reportedly won't suspend him, but that doesn't mean Pittsburgh can rely on a player who hasn't done much on the field and whose behavior is unreliable too.

There are also injury concerns at a key spot. Edge rusher Nick Herbig was inactive Sunday because of rib and hip injuries, then Alex Highsmith left the game against the Eagles early because of an ankle injury. The Steelers get the 8-2 Broncos on Friday and the Texans and Jaguars after that. Pittsburgh was once 6-2. It's possible it will be under .500 by mid-December.

David Montgomery could finally make a big impact for the Texans. In his return from injury, he rushed for 107 yards on 26 carries against the Colts. Indianapolis isn't a good team but it was still nice to see something positive from Houston's running game, even if it was in a blowout.

The Texans have been looking for consistency all season, but it's not too late for them to rally for a wild-card spot in a weak race. Their Week 13 game at the Steelers will be a big one for the Texans' playoff hopes. For now, Houston hopes a dominant win over Indianapolis is the start of a streak.

"It's huge," quarterback C.J. Stroud said, according to the team's site. "I think this is a start to something that we need to go on a run with."

Jayden Daniels is still capable of looking like a superstar at quarterback. When the Commanders looked like they had lost to the Bengals on a field goal with 46 seconds left, Daniels hit two passes to rookie Antonio Williams for a total of 64 yards, which set up a game-winning field goal as time expired. They were two great throws from Daniels and a great job by Williams to get open. Daniels finished with 289 yards, 122 of which went to Williams.

The Commanders remain two games behind the Giants in the NFC East. But Daniels and Williams kept the Commanders' season alive with two great plays in the final minute on Monday night.

Baker Mayfield's injuries have played a big part in his quiet season, but the Buccaneers still need more from the passing game. Mayfield's top game this season is 243 yards. He had 187 yards against a vulnerable Lions defense on Sunday. Mayfield has just five passing touchdowns in 175 attempts. His yards per attempt of 6.3 is the lowest of his career.

Mayfield was playing through a foot injury Sunday. The Buccaneers need more out of the passing game because they can't keep dropping games and stay in the NFC South race. A loss Monday night to the Panthers might ruin their playoff hopes.

"We're out of mulligans," Mayfield said, according to the team's site.

It's weird to say after giving up 30 points at home to the Titans, but the Cowboys' defense looked better after Mike Pettine took over play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Almost all of the Titans' yards came when they were down double digits and trying to get back in the game. The Titans didn't score a touchdown in the first half.

"Very proud of those guys," Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said of the defense, according to the team's site. "I think the first half was outstanding, but I thought they did a great job of blocking out the noise and working. I was really excited for how they performed."

Fernando Mendoza played well, although his pick-6 in the fourth quarter with the game on the line was a rookie moment. Against a very good Broncos defense, Mendoza had 267 passing yards and three touchdowns. He also rushed for 22 yards. He played well despite being without superstar tight end Brock Bowers, who was out with an ankle injury. For a second NFL start, it was promising.

"He's a first-round pick, first overall for a reason," Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton said, via the team's transcripts. "He's going to be a good player."

The pick-6 just after the two-minute warning ended the Raiders' comeback hopes. There was still progress from Mendoza.

"I felt a lot more comfortable this week than last week," Mendoza said, via the team's site. "They're both great defenses, both top in the league. However, I just felt like I was able to settle in and was able to see the entire field better. I was able to see the entire football field."

Daniel Jones could remain an option for the Patriots after he was suddenly released by the Colts, though head coach Mike Vrabel wouldn't address that Monday. He said Tommy DeVito will start in Week 12.

"We're excited about that, good preseason, and Tommy's improved," Vrabel said.

DeVito struggled when he was forced into action against the Lions in Germany before the bye week. He gets to face the Chargers this weekend, which gives DeVito a chance to impress and keep the job. But it also wouldn't be surprising if Jones finishes the season for a Patriots team that is still in the playoff race.

Years from now, people will look back on the 2026 Ravens, see that Lamar Jackson missed most of the season and attribute Baltimore's poor record to that. And it won't be completely accurate. The defense, which is head coach Jesse Minter's specialty, has been miserable.

Over the Ravens' last five games they have allowed 35, 36, 33, 23 and 35 points. Baltimore lost all five of those games, and its losing streak is at six. Minter took the blame for the Panthers putting together a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, saying "It was just a poor job by me, and that's what it was." Players disagreed.

"I wouldn't necessarily agree with it, truthfully," linebacker Roquan Smith told the team's site. "I thought we were in some really good calls. It comes down to us doing our job. That has been the story all season."

The responsibility for a bad season still falls on Minter, who is in his first season as a head coach. Baltimore is 26th in the NFL in points allowed.

The Saints really don't do anything well. They're 21st in points scored per game and 22nd in yards gained, 23rd in points allowed and 27th in yards allowed. They're 16th in passing yards, 18th in passing yards allowed, 28th in rushing yards and 28th in rushing yards allowed. Even the passing yardage is not that great; Tyler Shough's yards per attempt of 6.2 is better than only four of the 32 qualified quarterbacks this season. Up and down their résumé, nothing stands out as a strength.

It has been a dreadful follow-up to a good second half to last season, which provided false hope for the Saints heading into this season. It looks like a multiple-year rebuild is still in the beginning stages. The good news is the Saints would have the eighth overall pick of the draft if the season ended now.

The problem with the Falcons isn't even their record because they play in the NFC South. But their upcoming schedule is at Vikings, vs. Lions and at Browns. Even one win in those three puts them at 4-9 with four to go. Atlanta will have to play a lot better to stay alive in the playoff hunt over the next three games.

The Falcons had a great two-game stretch against the Packers and Saints and also are the only team to beat the 49ers, so figuring out why they can't play that way most weeks has been tough.

"We got really good players, man," Falcons running back Bijan Robinson said, via the team's site. "Obviously, with the good players, you have to execute at a high level. We have to come together this week and tell ourselves, 'Is this how we want to end the season?'"

Sunday wasn't perfect for the Eagles, with just 214 yards on offense, but their defense is starting to play well. It allowed 255 yards in the 19-16 win over the Steelers, the second straight time the Eagles have held an opponent under 300 yards. Before that stretch, the Eagles hadn't held an opponent to fewer than 300 yards since Week 2, which was the last time Philadelphia had won a game before Sunday.

The Eagles will be tested against a very good Cowboys offense that is coming off a 51-point game against the Titans. But seeing the defense come through, with stellar linebacker play from Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell, gives them hope for a happy Thanksgiving.

The Jets have little to play for, and a loss to the Chargers would have put them in much better draft position next April, but winning is good for any NFL locker room. Even if it's against the Chargers.

"The thing is, a win is a win and that's what we look for and that's the way you play this game," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said, according to the team's site.

There have been some promising developments in the Jets' season, and probably none bigger than the play of edge rusher David Bailey, the second overall pick of the draft. Bailey had two more sacks, giving him 9.5 for the season. Jevon Kearse set the rookie record with 14.5 and Bailey is on pace to break that, though in a 17-game season. He has been undeniably impressive and a big piece for a Jets team that has three first-round picks next year.

Nick Rallis always seemed like an awkward fit as the Cardinals' defensive coordinator, considering he wasn't successful in three previous seasons under an old regime but was retained. First-year head coach Mike LaFleur fired him Monday after another disappointing performance. The Cardinals are 31st in expected points added allowed per play, ahead of only the Cowboys.

The Cardinals haven't been good on defense, but talent certainly seems to be lacking. Safety Budda Baker, the one star the defense has, leads the team with 3.5 sacks. That's a terrible sign. First-round picks up front, like Zaven Collins and Darius Robinson, haven't broken out. We're about to find out if that was because of a coaching problem.

The Colts cutting Daniel Jones less than 24 hours after his 11th straight start to begin the season was odd, even if it ensures they don't have to pay a 2027 injury guarantee. Jones was poor against the Texans, but he was poor all season. He's dead last among NFL starting quarterbacks in EPA per play this season. But the Colts didn't care before Week 11, starting Jones and seemingly never giving any serious consideration to benching him to at least get a look at Anthony Richardson Sr. Cutting a quarterback after starting him all season is a sign of a franchise that isn't making sound decisions.

At least the Colts now can get a look at Richardson, who showed some progress in the preseason. Richardson hasn't shown many signs that he can be an NFL starter, but it's not like the Colts are losing anything by taking another look.

The Dolphins haven't been dominated often. They were dominated Sunday, when they fell behind early and got crushed by a superior Bills team.

One positive point from Sunday was another big game from rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, who had 13 tackles and an interception. He has 93 tackles, a pair of interceptions and a sack this season. Rodriguez was a tremendous college player but he fell to the second round of the NFL Draft. He has already shown that his production at Texas Tech was no fluke and gives the Dolphins one foundational piece in what is going to be a long rebuild.

There wasn't much to be happy with after Sunday's blowout loss. Cam Ward's final line didn't look terrible, but in the first half against a Cowboys defense that is worst in the NFL in many categories, Ward had 55 passing yards and the Titans didn't score a touchdown.

The defense was even worse, giving up 51 points. In Tennessee's last four games it has allowed 491, 510, 459 and 480 yards. The defense was supposed to be much better under head coach Robert Saleh, and it is one of the worst in the NFL. Tennessee has allowed more yards per game than any other team.

"These last couple of weeks, I'm not going to try and sugarcoat anything," Saleh said Monday, according to the team's site. "It's been dog s***."

Good thing the Chargers got that win in Week 10. Losing to the Jets on Sunday at home was a strong indication that Los Angeles might not win again.

At least there were a couple of decent performances on offense. Omarion Hampton continued to get hot late in the season with 89 rushing yards. Justin Herbert had a 119.3 passer rating. His best mark in a game this season before Sunday was 87.5. Unfortunately, Herbert landed in concussion protocol after the loss. Ladd McConkey has had an injury-filled and unproductive season but he had two touchdowns against the Jets. It's not much, especially in a loss. But it's not like there have been many other positives for the Chargers.

#2547. Camilo Duran attracting Premier League interest

Camilo Duran of Celtic celebrates scoring Celtic v St Mirren, Scottish Premiership, , Celtic Park – 21 November 2026. Photo Mark Runnacles Shutterstock IMAGO

Celtic striker Camilo Duran has more than proved his worth after signing for the club in a £6 million deal from Qarabag in the summer.

The Colombian has scored 14 goals and provided six assists in all competitions so far this campaign, and is naturally attracting attention from other clubs, with one club south of the border recently sending scouts to have a closer look at the 24 year old in action.

21.11.2026 Celtic v St.Mirren, Scottish Premiership : Camilo Duran scores 2-0 Photo Kenny Ramsay IMAGO

#2543. The Bills have a new path to the one seed after the Bengals’ loss

The Buffalo Bills took care of business against an underdog on Sunday, beating the Miami Dolphins. The Jacksonville Jaguars and Cincinnati Bengals both lost to underdogs from the NFC East on Sunday and Monday, which paves the way for the Bills to clinch the number one seed in a new scenario.

Yes, with seven games left it is premature to talk about clinching scenarios, but the Bills have a four-game lead in the AFC East plus two games left against the Jets and Dolphins. The division crown is heavily tilted toward the Bills now, and we are starting to look past that to the one seed. (The Bills are obvously focused one game at a time.)

With the Jaguars and Bengals losing this week, the Bills now can win the rest of their AFC games and secure the overall record and the AFC record they would need to clinch the one seed, a status that has eluded them throughout Josh Allen's entire career.

Buffalo has games against the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and New England Patriots plus the Dolphins and Jets. Winning those five AFC contests gets them to 14 wins and an 11-1 AFC record with head-to-head tiebreakers over the Broncos and Chiefs. Denver and KC would both have three losses on account of losing to Buffalo. Meanwhile the Jaguars and Bengals could top out at 14-3 but have two AFC losses apiece. Even in a three-way tie scenario, the Bills would come out on top.

In short, if the Bills win the rest of their AFC games, they can lose both games to the NFC North's Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers and still be the one seed in the AFC. (Winning those is preferable, but irrelevant here.)

If the Bills stumble against an AFC opponent, obviously things will need to be recalibrated. Regardless, the Bengals' loss on Monday is a win for the Bills.

#2542. San Antonio vs. Sacramento, Final Score: Short-handed Spurs scorch the nets in 123-107 win

Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, and Tobias Harris sat shoulder to shoulder, decked out in designer clothes, on the sidelines of the Golden 1 Center. Typically, the San Antonio Spurs would need them to don their uniforms to win a game, but that wasn't necessary on Monday night. Down four key rotation players, the Spurs took down the Sacramento Kings at home 123-107.

The Spurs played an analytical game, taking a lot of threes and frequently getting to the free-throw line. San Antonio knocked down 16 of their 46 three-pointers, and shot 23-for-25 from the stripe. The Spurs pulled out a double-digit victory despite being outscored in the paint 54-46.

Without a majority of the starting lineup, Stephon Castle led the Spurs with a near triple-double. Castle led all scorers with 28 points and added 8 rebounds and 11 assists, all while turning the ball over only twice. The Kings elected not to guard Castle from three, and he made them pay, shooting four-for-eight from deep.

Domantas Sabonis led the way for the Kings with 20 points, 12 rebounds and 8 assists on an efficient 8-for-9 shooting from the field. He carved the Spurs up inside, but wasn't able to provide enough defensively to keep Sacramento in the game.

San Antonio has now won three straight games. They'll look to keep their winning streak alive in an important NBA Cup game against the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday night.

Julian Champagnie's hot shooting in the second quarter opened up a big lead for the Spurs. He hit five three-pointers in the frame and then didn't make another for the rest of the game. Champagnie scored 20 of his 22 points in the first half.

Keldon Johnson's passing continues to be one of the best new wrinkles in San Antonio's offensive attack. He's found great touch on lobs, especially after forcefully getting downhill on a drive. He tallied five assists, including an alley-oop that led to a thunderous Luke Kornet jam late in the fourth quarter.

Kornet filled in admirably for Wembanyama, just as he did last season. Kornet had a double-double with 18 points and 11 rebounds. He served as a big target on lob attempts in the pick-and-roll and fought for position on the offensive glass. Maybe a game like this is what he needed to find his rhythm for the rest of the season.

Tarris Reed Jr. played substantial minutes for the first time this season and got better as the game went along. Early on, he looked out of position and a bit timid, but as he got used to the pace of the game, he settled in and looked a lot more comfortable. Reed Jr. had 7 points, 7 rebounds, and 2 blocks in 15 minutes. One area where Reed Jr. thrived was on the glass, where he used his big body to clear out space and gobble up rebounds. He picked up three offensive boards in his limited playing time.

The Spurs' best offensive play against the Kings was the pick-and-roll, particularly with Castle handling and Kornet screening. Castle made some great reads to find shooters wide open in the corner as the Kings overhelped to contest Kornet in the paint. When Sacramento adjusted, Castle was able to get ot the basket or find his big man on lobs.

Ja'Kobi Gillespie played some excellent on-ball defense against Malik Monk at the end of the third quarter. He stayed in front of him and forced a bad shot. Overall, the rookie guard looked solid in his first meaningful NBA action. He had 3 points (a catch-and-shoot three), 4 assists, and a steal with no turnovers in 15 minutes. San Antonio desperately needed another player who could handle the ball and run the pick-and-roll on Monday. Gillespie filled in admirably.

David Jones-Garcia checked in during the second quarter, air-balled a three, then was subbed out and didn't return until the final moment of garbage time, when he knocked down a mid-range jumper.

San Antonio checked in a super small-ball lineup in the fourth quarter with Harrison Barnes playing center. It did not work and allowed the Kings to cut the lead to single digits. The Spurs put the starters back in and extended the lead, and the game never got to single digits again.

#2541. MLB rumors: Orioles narrow down search in hunt for starting pitchers; reliever market heating up

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving. In Major League Baseball, that usually means a slow news week. Those of us wanting a flurry of moves before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 are starting to lose a little hope, but hey, it's still possible. We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.

As for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov. 16, let's go.

The Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson.

Rogers is the best option here. He finished last season with a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts. CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 3 free agent this offseason and the best non-Tarik Skubal pitcher on the market. Here's part of the write-up:

Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.

As things stand, the Orioles' rotation starts with right-handers Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Cade Povich is a left-handed option, but they'd clearly like someone else who could qualify as a frontline starter from the left-handed side.

Former Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara has been involved in trade rumors for years and the Marlins never end up moving him. More of the same this offseason? Probably.

"I expect Sandy to be on the Marlins next year," general manager Peter Bendix told MLB Network.

Alcantara, 31, was 13-11 with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153 strikeouts in an MLB-best 214 innings last season. He also grabbed three saves down the stretch as the Marlins started experimenting with using starters in relief on their bullpen day between starts. The 2022 Cy Young winner missed all of 2024 after having Tommy John surgery and started to show flashes of his old self last season. He's now making $21 million in 2027 before hitting free agency.

If the Marlins contend, he'll surely stay put, but if they fall out of contention, it'll be another round of trade rumors.

Free agent left-hander A.J. Minter is getting a lot of interest, per MLB Network. Coming off a season in which he was productive for both the Mets and Twins (in all, a 2.56 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 41 strikeouts in 45 ⅔ innings), he's being chased by at least the Blue Jays, Nationals, Phillies, Rangers and Royals.

Though he's closed on occasion, Minter has been a quality setup man for most of his 10 MLB years, especially with the Braves in the 2020-24 range. He has good playoff numbers, too, with a 2.88 ERA in 20 career postseason appearances.

The Brewers have acquired right-handed reliever Ryan Walker from the Giants for two minor-league pitchers, the team announced late Sunday. Walker, 30, was up and down in his four years with the Giants, which included time as a closer. He had a 1.91 ERA, 10 saves and 2.8 WAR in 2024, but lost the job of closer during a sub-par 2025 season. Last year, he pitched to a 7.16 ERA and 1.81 WHIP in 32 ⅔ innings.

We have plenty of examples of the Brewers buying low on a player and ending up getting the best version of him, so Walker is the latest to keep an eye on here.

#2538. Commanders stun Bengals on walk-off field goal as Jayden Daniels leads improbable drive

LANDOVER, Md. — Jayden Daniels and the Commanders had scored on five consecutive drives, all of them covering 50 yards or more. But their last possession was the most daunting.

After the Cincinnati Bengals took a one-point lead on a 56-yard field goal by Evan McPherson, Washington took over at its 28-yard line with 39 seconds left and no timeouts. The Commanders' defense had kept them in the game, but now it was up to Daniels.

The third-year quarterback made two pinpoint throws to rookie Antonio Williams, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens' 26-yard field goal as time expired, and Washington stunned Joe Burrow and the Bengals 22-20 on Monday night.

Jayden Daniels of the Washington Commanders celebrates defeating the Cincinnati Bengals in Landover, Md., Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. Getty Images

"Win the game, do whatever it takes to win the game," Daniels said. "I personally live for those moments. High-pressure situations. Being able to have the chance, back against the wall, 40-something seconds. … It just means a lot."

Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati 8. The QB spiked it with 5 seconds left and Stevens converted his fifth field goal of the night, all in the second half.

Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn celebrates after winning an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals in Landover, Md., Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. AP Photo/Nick Wass

Daniels finished with 283 yards passing and led the team with 55 yards rushing, and Williams had nine catches for 122 yards as Washington (4-5-1) remained in the NFC East race, two games behind the division-leading New York Giants.

The Commanders became the first NFL team in at least 30 years to end a game with six consecutive scoring drives that each covered more than 50 yards, according to OptaSTATS. Only one of them concluded with a touchdown.

"This was a full team win," coach Dan Quinn said.

Burrow threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns for AFC North-leading Cincinnati (7-3), but the Commanders largely held in check a Bengals team that had won five straight, scoring 31 points or more each time. Washington's defense forced Burrow to settle for checkdowns all night and mostly prevented big plays from the dangerous receiving duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

"They did their normal — we just didn't pick it up and execute it the right way," Chase said.

Drew Stevens (19) of the Washington Commanders celebrates with teammates after kicking a game-winning field goal on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, in Landover, Md. Getty Images

Chase and Higgins combined for just seven catches for 74 yards.

"This is an easy team to play zone and play it safe," Quinn said. "If you do that, they're likely to rip you. It's hard to challenge, but in my opinion, that was what was best for us."

Quinn made another questionable late-game decision when he sent Stevens out on fourth-and-1 to kick a 41-yard field goal with 2:26 left for a 19-17 lead. That left plenty of time for Burrow, who found Mike Gesicki for a 32-yard completion to move the Bengals into field goal range.

The Commanders' defense came through again with a sack to push the Bengals back, and McPherson made the long kick with 46 seconds left. As it turned out, that was too much time.

Chase said the toughest part about Cincinnati's winning streak ending was "losing when you know you're better."

The game got off to a slow start in unexpected rainy conditions, but opened up in the second half as the teams traded scores throughout the third quarter. Burrow's 4-yard touchdown pass to Colbie Young put the Bengals ahead 17-10, and the Commanders rallied with three field goals by Stevens.

Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) is helped up after being sacked during an NFL football game against the Washington Commanders in Landover, Md. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson

"At some point defenses are going to make plays too," Gesicki said. "I think everybody was so accustomed to the Bengals scoring 30-plus and blah blah blah, everybody wants to talk about it. Listen, it's the National Football League. They are going to make plays and stuff's going to happen."

There was an unexpected stoppage early in the third when the stadium lights went out with the Commanders in the red zone. After a delay that lasted about four minutes, Stevens converted from 36 yards to tie the game at 10-all.

The Bengals had already missed some key opportunities by then.

"I just thought we didn't start very well," coach Zac Taylor said. "They found some momentum early in the game and they came after us and we didn't really do a great job providing the answers until the third, fourth drive."

Washington held Cincinnati to three points on its first four possessions before Higgins' 31-yard touchdown catch that made it 10-0. Jacory Croskey-Merritt, activated off injured reserve earlier Monday, scored on a 1-yard run for the Commanders with 12 seconds left before halftime.

Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle, left, and Minnesota Timberwolves forward Jaden McDaniels talk after a game Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, in Minneapolis. AP Photo/Matt Krohn
